doc.citation: Rodrigues, L.C., do Carmo, D., Assine, M. and Steemans, P. (2022). Cryptospores of Iapó formation: The first evidence of early land plants from Late Ordovician in Paraná Basin, Brazil. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 305, 104742.
doc.comment: New Iapó Formation records; comparisons and historical geographical distributions are not treated as newly sampled assemblages. Twelve species are shared with the Vila Maria Formation assemblage previously reported by Mizusaki et al. (2002), rather than identified as reused specimens. The claimed five productive samples conflict with six sample codes carrying spore records. Captions, systematic accounts and Fig. 5 contain conflicting sample assignments, noted below. Aldeia is retained at section scope because Rugosphaera cerebra is reported there without a sample assignment. Reworking is not discussed.

items.age_basis_detail: Lithostratigraphic correlation with Hirnantian glacial deposits of the Zapla and Cancañiri formations; formation-level age additionally supported by the brachiopod Kosoidea australis and ostracode Harpabolia harparum.
items.notes: Only one Aldeia sample was productive, with very low palynomorph recovery. The systematic accounts explicitly assign Tetrahedraletes medinensis, Laevolancis chibrikovae and Gneudnaspora divellomedia var. minor to MP 2849. MP 3490, MP 2851 and MP 2852 were analysed but have no reported recovery. Rugosphaera cerebra includes Aldeia only in its geographical distribution statement, without a specimen or sample assignment. MP 2849 is described as basal diamictite in §3 but as upper diamictite in the T. medinensis account; its slide is reported damaged there. Marine palynomorphs were also sought.

items.setting_as_reported: siltstone lens contained in stratified diamictite; glaciomarine environment; internal neritic system
items.notes: Basal assemblage, with marine acritarchs, Tortotubus protuberans and abundant opaque fragments. Replicate preparations were made in Brasília and Liège. Several plate captions give this sample's height as 2.3 m or 2,3 m, whereas §3 and the systematic horizons give 2.6 m. Segestrespora laevigata and Velatitetras rugosa are assigned to MP 3384 by their systematic accounts, but their illustrated specimens are assigned to MP 3386 in the captions. Rare unusually large Segestrespora rugosa specimens occur only in MP 3384; their taxonomic distinction is unresolved. The illustrated Polyad is additional to the 17 named cryptospore species.
